questions.stem: Who was the FOUNDER of the Maratha Empire, crowned 'Chhatrapati' in 1674?
questions.explanation: SHIVAJI BHONSLE (1630-1680) — founded the Maratha Empire from his base in the Deccan. Born at SHIVNERI FORT (Maharashtra) to Shahaji Bhonsle + JIJABAI (a formidable influence on his upbringing). Began by capturing Torna Fort at age 17 (1646). Expanded by 'ganimi kava' (guerrilla warfare). KEY EVENTS: (1) 1659 — killed Afzal Khan (Adil Shahi general) with WAGHNAKH ('tiger claws') at Pratapgad; (2) 1666 — imprisoned by Aurangzeb at Agra, escaped in fruit baskets; (3) 1674 — CROWNED CHHATRAPATI at RAIGAD FORT in a grand Vedic ceremony performed by Gaga Bhatt of Kashi, on 6 June 1674 (SHIV RAJYABHISHEK). Established EIGHT MINISTERS (ASHTAPRADHAN) council — Peshwa (PM), Amatya (Finance), Mantri (Interior), Senapati (Commander), Sachiv (Correspondence), Sumant (Foreign Affairs), Nyayadhish (Chief Justice), Panditrao (Religious Affairs). Forts: RAIGAD (capital), SINHAGAD, PURANDAR, PRATAPGAD, RAJGAD. Died 3 April 1680. Succeeded by son SAMBHAJI (captured + tortured + executed by Aurangzeb 1689).

questions.stem: The TREATY OF PURANDAR (1665) was signed between Shivaji and which Mughal general?

options.option_text: Raja Jai Singh I of Amber

questions.explanation: TREATY OF PURANDAR (June 1665) — signed between SHIVAJI + RAJA JAI SINGH I OF AMBER (Amer/Jaipur, Rajput general under Aurangzeb). Jai Singh's Mughal force besieged Purandar Fort; after heavy fighting, Shivaji accepted terms: (1) Surrendered 23 of his 35 forts to Mughals; (2) Agreed to serve as a mansabdar of 5000 with his son Sambhaji; (3) Paid tribute + kept only 12 forts (collective revenue 1 lakh huns); (4) Assisted Mughals against Bijapur. As part of this, Shivaji visited Agra in 1666 where he was insulted by Aurangzeb (placed in a lower rank). Imprisoned — famously ESCAPED on 19 August 1666, hidden in fruit/sweet baskets with his son. EARLIER generals Aurangzeb sent: SHAISTA KHAN (Shivaji's maternal uncle by marriage, infamous raid on Lal Mahal Pune 1663 — Shivaji chopped off his fingers in a night raid); AFZAL KHAN (Adil Shahi, killed at Pratapgad 1659). LATER: Pronounced war 1670 onwards, Shivaji sacked SURAT TWICE (1664, 1670) — richest Mughal port.

questions.stem: After Shivaji + Sambhaji's deaths, the Maratha polity was transformed into a CONFEDERACY under the PESHWAS. The most powerful Peshwa (1720-1740) who established Maratha supremacy in northern India was:

options.option_text: BAJI RAO I (1720-1740) — never lost a battle in his 20-year career

questions.explanation: BAJI RAO I (Bajirao Ballal, 1700-1740) — 7th Peshwa (first among the Chitpavan Brahmin Peshwas to wield full power). Ruled 1720-1740. Expanded Maratha power from Deccan to Delhi. Famous for: (1) Guerrilla warfare mastery — UNDEFEATED in 41 battles; (2) Strategy: 'Strike at the trunk of the withering tree (Mughals); the branches will fall off themselves'; (3) Military campaigns: defeated Nizam-ul-Mulk of Hyderabad at PALKHED (1728); raided Delhi (1737, reached Red Fort); took Malwa + Bundelkhand + Gujarat; fought the BATTLE OF BHOPAL (1737) vs combined Nizam forces — Maratha victory. (4) Personal life: Married Kashibai + later MASTANI (Muslim/half-Muslim princess, scandalous at the time, immortalised in Bhansali's 2015 film 'Bajirao Mastani'). Died young (1740, age 39) of heatstroke/sudden illness at Raver camp. Succeeded by son BALAJI BAJI RAO (Nana Saheb, 1740-1761). Marathas reached zenith under him but then PANIPAT III DISASTER (14 Jan 1761) vs Ahmad Shah Abdali — broke the expansion.

questions.stem: The THIRD BATTLE OF PANIPAT (14 January 1761) was fought between the MARATHAS and:

options.option_text: Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani) of Afghanistan + Rohilla + Awadh allies

questions.explanation: THIRD BATTLE OF PANIPAT — 14 January 1761, at Panipat (Haryana). MARATHAS under SADASHIV RAO BHAU (Peshwa's cousin) + VISHWAS RAO (young heir apparent) + MALHAR RAO HOLKAR, MAHADJI SCINDIA, etc. vs AHMAD SHAH ABDALI (DURRANI) from Afghanistan + Indian allies: NAJIB-UD-DAULA (Rohilla), SHUJA-UD-DAULA (Nawab of Awadh). Maratha force ~45,000 soldiers + massive refugee camp. Outcome: MARATHAS DEVASTATED — ~40,000 killed in battle + 40,000 captives later massacred. Both Sadashiv Rao Bhau + Vishwas Rao killed. Peshwa Nana Saheb died of shock 6 months later. SIGNIFICANCE: Ended Maratha dream of replacing Mughals as paramount power; created vacuum for British East India Company expansion (started 4 years later at Battle of Buxar 1764). Abdali's victory didn't translate to lasting rule in India — he retreated. Sadashiv Rao Bhau's body never found — legend he survived (multiple imposter claims). Maratha historian Govind Sakharam Sardesai called this battle 'the saddest day in the history of India'.

questions.stem: The MARATHA CONFEDERACY post-Panipat was a loose federation of autonomous chiefs. Which of the following was NOT a major Maratha chieftain family?
questions.explanation: MARATHA CONFEDERACY (post-Panipat) — five major chieftainships ('Panchayatana'): (1) PESHWAS of PUNE — nominal overall leaders (Bhatt family, Chitpavan Brahmins); (2) SCINDIAS of GWALIOR (Madhya Pradesh) — founded by Ranoji Scindia; famous descendant Mahadji Scindia; (3) HOLKARS of INDORE (MP) — founded by Malhar Rao Holkar; famous AHILYABAI HOLKAR (queen-regent 1767-95 — great patron of temples, built ghats + temples at Varanasi, Somnath, Haridwar, Dwarka, etc.); (4) GAEKWADS of BARODA (Gujarat) — still continues as Baroda royal family (titular); (5) BHONSLES of NAGPUR (Maharashtra — different from Shivaji's Bhonsle line). The NIZAM of HYDERABAD was NOT Maratha — he was a Mughal-descended ruler (Asaf Jahi dynasty, independent from 1724 under Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I). Marathas extracted CHAUTH (1/4 revenue) + SARDESHMUKHI (1/10 revenue) from rulers who wanted protection / non-invasion. By early 19th c., weakened by internal conflicts + Anglo-Maratha wars (1775-82, 1803-05, 1817-18), British annexed them one by one.

questions.stem: The THREE ANGLO-MARATHA WARS (1775-82, 1803-05, 1817-18) culminated in the complete defeat of the Marathas. The LAST Peshwa, BAJI RAO II, surrendered after which war + retired where?

options.option_text: 3rd Anglo-Maratha War (1818); exiled to BITHUR (near Kanpur, UP) on pension
Battle of Panipat; retired to Gwalior

questions.explanation: BAJI RAO II — the LAST (13th) Peshwa (r. 1795-1818). Signed the TREATY OF BASSEIN (1802) with British — a Subsidiary Alliance, ceding authority — which triggered 2nd Anglo-Maratha War (1803-05). Defeated in 1st Anglo-Maratha War (partial). Defeated + exiled after 3rd ANGLO-MARATHA WAR (1817-18 — actually the Peshwa-led 'war' ended 1818). Signed Treaty of Poona (1817) surrendering power. The PESHWAI was formally ABOLISHED in 1818 by Lord Hastings. Baji Rao II was exiled to BITHUR (near Kanpur, UP) on a pension of ₹8 lakh/year. He lived there till his death in 1851. His adopted son NANA SAHEB (Dhondu Pant) was denied the pension continuation by Dalhousie — a key grievance that made Nana a leader of the 1857 Revolt. LATER Marathas: SATARA annexed 1848 (Doctrine of Lapse); NAGPUR 1854; JHANSI 1853. Saw themselves as successors to Shivaji via the Bhonsle line. Maharashtra's identity post-Shivaji became powerfully anti-imperial.

options.option_text: Lord of the umbrella / Supreme sovereign (umbrella-bearer, symbol of kingship)

questions.explanation: CHHATRAPATI = 'Chhatra' (umbrella / royal canopy) + 'Pati' (master/lord) = 'Lord of the Umbrella' — a symbol of sovereign kingship in Indian tradition (the umbrella is an ancient Sanskrit royal insignia, going back to Vedic times). Hence CHHATRAPATI = Supreme Sovereign / Paramount Ruler. The title put Shivaji on par with (or superior to) Mughal Padshah + Adil Shah + Nizam — asserting Maratha independence. The coronation ceremony on 6 June 1674 at Raigad was performed by GAGA BHATT (Pandit Vishwanath Bhatt of Banaras), who after initial objections (Marathas not being ritualistic Kshatriyas) agreed to perform a Vedic RajyaAbhishek. A second Tantric Abhishek was also done later. Shivaji adopted new regnal insignia: his own coinage (HOH / HONS / SHIVRAI), royal seal in Sanskrit, titles like HAINDAVA-DHARMODDHAARAKA (Defender of Hindu Dharma), MARATHA MAHAMARATHA. Modern Indian railway stations + international airport in Mumbai named after him (CSMT — Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, 1996 renaming; CSMIA airport). Hon'd with national importance post-independence.
